page: Microsoft Azure B8als_v2 is a burstable general-purpose virtual machine based on the AMD EPYC 7763 processor running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance provisions 8 burstable vCPUs derived from 4 physical x86_64 cores with multithreading enabled, operating at a base frequency of 3.525 GHz. System memory is sized at 16.0 GB, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio corresponding to Azure's low-memory profile. The CPU architecture includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, supporting standard instruction sets including AES, VAES, SHA-NI, and AVX.

Hardware accelerators are absent, with zero GPUs allocated, and the instance includes no local storage, requiring attached network volumes for persistent storage and operating system files. In benchmark evaluations, the single-core CPU execution ranks strong within the top quartile during stress-ng testing. Multi-core performance across Geekbench and PassMark suites registers within median industry distributions, reflecting the shared burstable processor design. Memory subsystem throughput remains consistent, delivering 101.84 GB/s in large block sequential reads and 62.89 GB/s in write benchmarks, though multi-threaded decompression tasks exhibit lower relative throughput.

The burstable CPU model confers distinct qualitative cost efficiency, allowing organizations to avoid the premium of dedicated sustained compute when workload patterns are irregular. The lower memory-to-core ratio introduces a tradeoff, restricting suitability for large in-memory datasets or memory-heavy enterprise databases. The configuration functions effectively for continuous integration and build agents, intermediate web application serving, staging systems, and microservices experiencing fluctuating request volumes.
description: Microsoft Azure B8als_v2 is a burstable virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at 3.525 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 8 burstable vCPUs across 4 physical cores, 16.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU), and no bundled local storage or GPUs, utilizing external storage solutions instead. Its compute profile demonstrates strong single-core stress-ng performance while maintaining mid-tier results in multi-core PassMark, Geekbench, and memory bandwidth benchmarks. The burstable credit model offers cost efficiency for applications that experience variable or intermittent load patterns rather than sustained core saturation. With a reduced memory-to-core ratio and solid baseline throughput, B8als_v2 is well configured for development and staging environments, lightweight web servers, software build pipelines, and low-concurrency database operations.
